message.content: can you add a feild to the bills feature page to upload an invoice and then on the check out page for any bill being sent that isnt rent, can you add a text line hyper link saying view invoice which allows them to click it and it takes them to the invoice which they can download, share etc

content.text: Yes, that's very doable, and it fits patterns already in this codebase. Here's how it breaks down — note I'm answering from context only, so treat the file/field names as the shape to confirm rather than verified facts. ## 1. Upload field on the bills/charge page You already have a working file-upload pattern to copy: the logo uploader in `settings.tsx` (`uploadLogoMutation`) posts `FormData` to `POST /api/merchants/:id/logo` and the server stores it and returns a URL. The bills/one-off-charge form (the page behind the recent "create one-off charges" work) would get the same treatment: - A file input (``) with a small preview/filename chip, gated so it only shows when the charge **isn't rent** (i.e. for one-off/non-rent bills). - On submit, upload the file (multipart) to an endpoint like `POST /api/property/invoices/:id/document` (or include it in the charge-creation request), get back a stored URL. - Persist that URL on the invoice record — a new column such as `invoiceDocumentUrl` (and maybe `invoiceDocumentName`) on the invoices table in `storage.ts` / the schema. This is the one piece that needs a DB/schema change and a migration. ## 2. "View invoice" link on the checkout page On `checkout.tsx`, for any bill being sent **where it's not rent and `invoiceDocumentUrl` exists**, render a text hyperlink: ```jsx {!isRent && invoice.invoiceDocumentUrl && ( View invoice )} ``` Opening the file URL in a new tab gives the user native **download/share** (browser PDF viewer → download; on mobile the share sheet). If you want an explicit in-app share, you can wrap it with the Web Share API (`navigator.share({ url })`) falling back to the plain link. The "isn't rent" condition depends on how rent vs. one-off bills are distinguished on the invoice model — likely a `type`/`kind` field or the presence of a rent schedule link. That's the key thing to pin down in the data model. ## What's needed end-to-end 1. **Schema**: add `invoiceDocumentUrl` (+ optional name) to invoices. 2. **Server**: an upload endpoint storing the file (reuse whatever object storage the logo route uses) + include the URL when invoices are returned to the checkout page. 3. **Bills page**: conditional file-upload field for non-rent charges. 4. **Checkout page**: conditional "View invoice" link styled in the navy design. If you'd like this built, the main agent (working separately) can pick it up — the cleanest first step is confirming the invoice "type" flag and the existing file-storage route so the upload reuses them rather than inventing a new mechanism.

Done. Implemented the invoice-attachment feature end-to-end, preserving all existing behaviour.

**What I built**
1. **Bills page upload field** (`ChargeBill` screen in `property-terminal.tsx`): an optional "attach invoice (PDF/image)" control under the description. On file pick it uploads immediately, shows the filename with a "remove" option, and the stored URL is attached when the bill is sent. Draft state survives the keypad round-trip and resets after send / on cancel, matching the existing charge-draft pattern.
2. **Checkout link** (`checkout.tsx`): for any non-rent bill (`kind === "charge"`) that has a document, a centred "View invoice" hyperlink appears under the amount. It opens the file in a new tab, giving the payer native view/download/share. It does not render for rent or for charges without an attachment.

**Plumbing**
- `shared/schema.ts`: added `documentUrl` / `documentName` columns to `invoices_rent_requests` and the matching optional fields to `createAdHocInvoiceSchema`.
- `server/routes.ts`: added a multer config (PDF/PNG/JPEG/WebP/HEIC, 20 MB) writing to `uploads/invoices` (served by the existing static `/uploads` mount), a new authenticated `POST /api/property/invoices/document` endpoint returning `{ documentUrl, documentName }`, and added `documentUrl`/`documentName` to the public `GET /api/checkout/resolve/:token` response. The existing create route already spreads the parsed fields into `createInvoiceRentRequest`, so they persist with no storage change.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` shows **42 errors before and after** my changes — zero introduced, none referencing any new identifier. All 42 are pre-existing (checkout ES5 function-in-block / global-modifier issues, unrelated routes.ts enum and `merchantId` typings).

Files changed (not committed): `shared/schema.ts`, `server/routes.ts`, `client/src/pages/property/property-terminal.tsx`, `client/src/pages/checkout.tsx`.

**Two things to action before this works in a running env** (outside my scope to run safely): the new DB columns require `npm run db:push` against the database; and I did not start the app for a live click-through, so a manual smoke test of upload → send → checkout link is still worth doing.
